title: adaptive-horizon-throttler-continuous-batcher-with-kv-prefetch-elasticity
author: Aisha Raman
release_notes: Introduce an adaptive horizon throttler for continuous batching that reduces tail latency for short requests during KV-heavy bursts and adds a new configurable KV prefetch elasticity knob.
description:
Motivation: We observed repeated tail-latency spikes in hosted runs when a mix of long KV-heavy requests and latency-sensitive short requests share the continuous-batcher. Existing soft-reservations and slot decay reduced average latency but allowed starvation when long requests occupied kernels and KV pins for extended windows. This PR implements an "adaptive horizon throttler" that prevents starvation by combining a token-horizon admission window, stochastic slot jitter, and KV-prefetch elasticity so we can trade small amounts of throughput for large reductions in P95/P99 latency.

What this change does (single-string body): Adds a new scheduling layer to the continuous-batcher path that: (1) attaches a per-request "horizon" estimate derived from sequence-length metadata and observed service-time quantiles; (2) enforces an admission window that caps the cumulative horizon tokens in-flight per GPU worker; (3) introduces a small randomized admission jitter to prevent synchronization-induced bursts; (4) provides soft-preemption for queued short requests by allowing the scheduler to temporarily pause long request admission when short-request wait exceeds configured thresholds; (5) exposes a KV prefetch elasticity parameter that reduces aggressive KV pin prefetching when queue horizon is near saturation, reducing contention on KV memory and eviction churn; (6) surfaces new telemetry: horizon_in_flight, horizon_limit, preempt_count, kv_prefetch_shrink_events.

Implementation notes: The scheduler change is implemented in scheduler/continuous/batcher_horizon.go and integrated with the existing admission/coordinator layer. We keep the admission decision cheap: horizon tokens are computed from a small lookup table (+ simple moving average for runtime). The preemption path marks long inflight requests as "yieldable"; worker threads observe yieldable flags at kernel execution boundaries (safe yield points) and trigger continuation deferral. KV prefetch elasticity hooks into kv/prefetch_policy.go with a new policy that decays prefetch window when horizon_limit utilization > 0.8. All new knobs are feature-flagged behind runtime.featureFlags.AdaptiveHorizon so rollout can be staged.

Testing and validation: Unit tests cover horizon accounting and preemption state transitions. Integration tests simulate mixed workloads (short text gen 16 tokens, long kv-heavy 4096 tokens) and assert P95/P99 improvements. We added a deterministic scheduler simulator under scheduler/test_sim that allowed tuning of jitter and horizon limits. Benchmarks run on perf-canary show: P95 reduced by ~18% and P99 reduced by ~27% on KV-heavy mixes; throughput drop under steady long-only workloads is ~2.5% with default knobs.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear: ENG-5423) - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Perf microbench and perf-canary run - [x] Feature-flag gating - [x] Console telemetry and dashboard links added - [x] Release notes drafted

Rollout plan: Merge behind feature flag, roll to perf-canary, enable for 10% of hosted traffic, monitor horizon_in_flight & preempt_count and P99. If KV evictions increase, revert prefetch elasticity or tune shrink factor.

Related: This PR complements the KV prefetch tuning work in ENG-5487 and the recent slot-decay improvements. It is intended to be conservative: soft-preemption defers continuation rather than forcibly killing tasks and prefetch elasticity only shrinks windows when saturation is detected.

Notes on configuration: Default knobs were chosen to avoid visible throughput regressions for long-only jobs: horizon_limit_worker = 12000 tokens, jitter_ms = 3ms (exponential backoff cap 25ms), prefetch_shrink_factor = 0.6 when utilization > 0.8. All knobs are configurable via Operator CRD for Dedicated/Private installs.
